independent.summary: The new sweep-verdict pass treats the synthetic group URL as a swept page, so it writes/blanks scanRules on a real ScrapedPage row that happens to sit at that URL. getGroupUrl() maps `/staff/ann` → `https://d/staff/` and any root-level thin page → `https://d/` (the homepage), and tallyChunkCounts credits chunk.url, so the group URL always lands in chunkCountByUrl. When a group is rebuilt because one member changed and the group chunks trip nothing, the real `/staff/` (or home) page — unchanged, therefore absent from pageHashUpdates and never rescanned this run — falls into sweptCleared and its stored finding is overwritten with [], silently dropping a live warning chip for content that was not re-read; symmetrically a secret in a member card gets attributed to the index page. The code's own justification ("a page that contributed no chunk this run was NOT looked at") does not hold for the group key, and the pass guards only against minting a row, not against hitting an existing one.
